question:
A 25-year-old man who plays college lacrosse presents with a one-week history of malaise, headache,
fever, and sore throat that have made it impossible for him to participate in lacrosse practice. He has a
fever of 38.9°C, pharyngeal erythema and exudates, and tender posterior cervical adenopathy. His
spleen is not palpable. He is up to date with Covid-19 vaccinations, and testing for SARS-CoV-2 is
negative. A heterophile antibody latex agglutination and Epstein-Barr virus viral capsid antigen
immunoglobulin M and immunoglobulin G are positive. Which one of the following criteria best
determines when this athlete is likely to be able to safely return to full activity, including sports,
assuming resolution of symptoms? Answer Choices: (A) Normalization of liver function tests (B)
Resolution of cervical lymphadenopathy (C) Three weeks elapse after the onset of symptoms (D)
Seven weeks elapse after the onset of symptoms (E) Two consecutive negative heterophile antibody
tests (F) Return of normal exercise tolerance (G) An abdominal ultrasound confirms the absence of
splenomegaly (H) Negative EBV IgM antibodies (I) EBV viral load becomes undetectable (J) Complete
resolution of fatigue symptoms
 A. Negative EBV IgM antibodies

B. Three weeks elapse after the onset of symptoms
C. Return of normal exercise tolerance
D. Complete resolution of fatigue symptoms
E. EBV viral load becomes undetectable
F. An abdominal ultrasound confirms the absence of splenomegaly
G. Seven weeks elapse after the onset of symptoms
H. Two consecutive negative heterophile antibody tests
I. Resolution of cervical lymphadenopathy
J. Normalization of liver function tests
